Maya R: FYI I ran an apples-to-apples run comparing streaming vs non-streaming with our replay harness this morning. wanted to share odd perf regressions
Sam T: nice—what configs did you keep constant? batching, model, kernel selection?
Maya R: kept model/weights constant (gpt-7b-quant), same GPU type, identical prompt mix from replay. toggled: streaming enabled vs disabled, chunk_size 64/128/256, client read loop delays (0/5/20ms).
Kevin L: did you also freeze the batching policy? if we let auto-batching vary the throughput comparison isn't apples-to-apples.
Maya R: yep. disabled adaptive batching and forced batch size 1/4/8 for separate runs. also pinned kernel selection to cuBLAS vs fused-attn path to see kernel impact.
Priya S: curious about KV cache behavior—did you warm it? cold vs warmed cache can change p95 drastically for streaming since client gets early tokens while KV warms up.
Maya R: good call. I did cold-start runs and warm-start runs (1000 warmup reqs). warm had much lower p99 on non-streaming. streaming lowers initial TTFB for cold case but overall tail is weird.
perf-bot: summary: streaming v non-streaming sweep | model=gpt-7b-quant | gpu=A100 | batch=4 | chunk=128 | client-delay=5ms | p50/p95/p99 and tokens/s attached
Sam T: what did the tokens/sec look like? I expect streaming to be slightly lower due to chunk overhead if we do small chunks.
Maya R: tokens/s: nonstreaming ~ 12.3k tok/s, streaming (chunk=64) ~ 9.6k tok/s, streaming (chunk=256) ~ 11.8k tok/s. overhead from more small kernel launches plus backpressure on network read loops.
Kevin L: that matches intuition. also kernel selection matters: fused-attn path improved streaming with small chunks because it reduces kernel count per token.
Priya S: any profiling traces? nvprof/ CUPTI or our perf traces?
Maya R: attached flame traces in the replay harness output (link: https://ci.internal/replays/1763305555). shows spikes where client read loop blocks worker thread waiting for TCP flush. we saw ~6ms stalls in streaming read loop when chunk < 128.
Sam T: are those stalls in user-space or kernel-space? could be our epoll loop batching events into fewer wakeups.
Maya R: user-space. the client lib coalesces reads but if the app reads small chunks and then yields, the runtime thread sees sched delays.
Kevin L: for apples-to-apples, maybe measure end-to-end latency with synthetic traffic generator that honors same TCP read semantics for both streaming and non-streaming.
Maya R: I used our replay harness generator with two modes: synthetic closed-loop (client waits for each response) and replay-socket (faithful TCP pacing). results diverge significantly—closed-loop overestimates streaming perf.
Priya S: did you try switching to a background reader thread for streaming client to avoid blocking the main driver?
Maya R: yes. background reader reduced observed backpressure stalls by ~60% and tokens/s for streaming chunk=64 jumped to ~10.9k.
Sam T: kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache warmup all interact. any perf regressions after the recent kernel update?
Maya R: after the fused-kernel patch we saw 7% regression on non-streaming p95 in one config because the new kernel had worse small-batch perf. but for streaming small-chunk cases it improved.
Kevin L: suggests dynamic kernel selector should be workload-aware (streaming vs batch size distribution). maybe add simple heuristic: if avg chunk < 128 prefer fused, else full matmul.
Priya S: agree. also add KV-cache-warmup flag to tests so that CI can detect regressions that only show up in warm/cold combos.
Maya R: action items: 1) add background reader option to replay harness, 2) extend CI to run both cold and warm cache scenarios, 3) add a streaming-aware kernel selection heuristic, 4) document chunk size recommendations per GPU.
Sam T: I'll pick up CI changes. Kevin can prototype the kernel heuristic?
Kevin L: on it. will sketch a tiny decision tree based on avg_seq_len, avg_chunk_size, batch_size.
Maya R: thanks. will upload the raw traces and a small writeup with p50/p95/p99 tables in the replay artifact. please comment on thresholds. :thumbsup:
